content.text: Dallas Wrongful Death AttorneyWhen Negligence Causes a Permanent and Irreversible LossLosing a loved one because of someone else’s negligence is one of the most devastating experiences a family can endure. If your family is facing this kind of loss, you don’t have to navigate it alone. At Aldous Law, our team is here to support you and help you pursue justice and accountability. With decades of experience, our Dallas wrongful death attorneys provide compassionate, strategic guidance for families across Dallas and throughout Texas. You deserve answers, and your loved one’s story deserves to be heard. https://www.aldouslaw.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Clients-Are-Like-Family.mp4 What Is Considered a Wrongful Death in Texas? Under Texas law, wrongful death occurs when a person's death is caused by a wrongful act, neglect, carelessness, unskillfulness, or default of another individual or entity. Some common situations that lead to wrongful death cases include: Catastrophic injuries Medical malpractice Car accidents Motorcycle accidents Pedestrian accidents Bicycle accidents Construction accidents Defective products If you believe your loved one’s death could have been prevented, you may have legal grounds to pursue a wrongful death claim. Contact our personal injury attorneys to learn more about your options. Permanent Loss and Emotional Impact on Families At Aldous Law, we’ve spent years helping families in Dallas who have lost loved ones due to a variety of circumstances. Some of the most common cases we handle include: Truck accidents caused by driver fatigue, improper maintenance, or negligence. Mistakes in medical care, including misdiagnosis, surgical errors, or neglect in nursing homes. Workplace fatalities are particularly prevalent in high-risk industries like construction. Drunk driving accidents, where negligence led to unimaginable loss. Each situation is different, and we take the time to understand every single detail so we can advocate for what’s right. The Lifetime Financial Consequences of a Wrongful Death While no amount of money can replace a human life, the financial reality of a sudden death can be overwhelming for surviving members. A wrongful death often leaves a family facing a lifetime of economic challenges, particularly if the deceased was a primary provider. The lifetime financial consequences we help families address include: Lost Financial Support: The wages, benefits, and future earning capacity the deceased would have provided over their working life. End-of-Life Expenses: Including medical bills incurred prior to death and funeral or burial costs. Loss of Household Services: The tangible value of the support and care the deceased provided to the home and children. Our goal is to ensure you are not forced to endure financial hardship on top of your grief. We investigate every detail to establish the full economic impact on your family’s future. Seeking Full Compensation for Surviving Loved Ones If your family has lost a loved one due to someone else’s negligence, a Texas wrongful death attorney can help you pursue compensation for both financial and emotional losses. Wrongful death damages in Texas generally fall into three main categories: Economic Damages cover the tangible financial costs that resulted from your loved one’s passing. This can include medical expenses incurred before death, funeral and burial costs, and lost wages or benefits that your family depended on. Non-Economic Damages address the emotional and relational impact of the loss. Families may seek compensation for mental anguish, grief, and loss of companionship, care, or guidance. Spouses may also be entitled to damages for loss of consortium — the loss of the support, comfort, and intimacy that the deceased provided. Punitive Damages may be awarded in cases where the responsible party acted with gross negligence, recklessness, or intentional misconduct. These damages go beyond compensating the family and are intended to hold the wrongdoer accountable for particularly egregious behavior. Working with an experienced Texas wrongful death attorney ensures that your family can recover the full range of damages allowed under the law while receiving compassionate guidance throughout the legal process. How Long Do You Have to File a Wrongful Death Claim in Texas? The statute of limitations for wrongful death claims in Texas is two years from the date of death in most cases. However, there are exceptions, and starting the process sooner is always better. Waiting too long could mean losing your opportunity to hold the responsible party accountable. Why Choose Aldous Law for Your Texas Wrongful Death Case? At Aldous Law, we don’t just represent clients; we partner with families to ensure their voices are heard. Attorney Charla Aldous has tried over 200 cases and secured significant results, including a $25 million jury verdict for a drunk driving fatality. What sets us apart is: Compassionate Advocacy: We treat every client like family. Proven Results: Our track record speaks for itself. Dedication to Justice: We fight to ensure wrongdoers are held accountable. When you choose Aldous Law, you gain a team that genuinely cares about your loss and is committed to your future. Protecting Your Rights Experiencing the loss of a loved one due to someone else’s negligence is overwhelming, both emotionally and mentally. While nothing can replace your loved one, taking certain steps early can help protect your legal rights and strengthen a wrongful death claim. Gather all documentation related to the incident, including medical records, accident reports, police reports, and any correspondence with insurance companies. Accurate records are critical for establishing the facts of the case and supporting your claim. Speak with an experienced Texas wrongful death attorney as soon as possible. A skilled lawyer can guide you through the legal process, explain your rights, and help ensure that you receive the full compensation you are entitled to. Avoid speaking directly with insurance adjusters or signing any documents without first consulting your attorney. Insurance companies often aim to minimize payouts, and even small statements or agreements can affect your claim. By taking these steps and working with a knowledgeable Texas wrongful death attorney, you can focus on grieving and healing while your legal rights are fully protected. Talk to a Dallas Wrongful Death Attorney Today After the loss of a loved one, it may seem like an insult to your loved one's memory to seek financial compensation. We at Aldous Law would never suggest that any amount of compensation could replace the family member you lost. We know the pain you are experiencing cannot be eased with money. Our only goal is to ensure you are not overwhelmed with medical bills, funeral bills, or other expenses that resulted from your loved one's death. Losing a loved one is brutal: achieving justice on his or her behalf could help you find some peace, knowing that what happened to your loved one won’t happen to anyone else. Addressing the financial aspect of your loss means you can focus on being with your family and on healing—not on the financial hardship it has caused.
